title: Strongly Polynomial-Time Linear Programming Algorithm Answering Smale’s Ninth Problem
whyItMatters: Claims a deterministic strongly polynomial algorithm for linear programming with arbitrary real coefficients—resolving Smale’s 1998 Ninth Problem with a Lean 4 RAM formalization.
summary: Posted in OpenAI’s November 24 math release (family 380), this manuscript presents a deterministic algorithm solving any explicitly given linear program with arbitrary real coefficients in a number of arithmetic operations polynomial solely in the number of variables and constraints (independent of coefficient bit-lengths), while preserving polynomial bit-length on rational inputs. It returns exact primal–dual optimal pairs, improving rays, or sparse infeasibility certificates, and extends to convex quadratic programming and turn-based mean-payoff games.
technicalHighlights: Directly targets Smale’s Ninth Problem (1998)—whether linear programming admits a strongly polynomial algorithm.
Includes Lean 4 formalizations of strongly polynomial feasibility and optimization on fixed rational RAM programs, certifying primal–dual equality.
Released alongside a companion disproof of the Polynomial Hirsch Conjecture, proving strongly polynomial LP is achievable even though simplex edge-paths can be superpolynomial.
caveats: Fresh November 24 unrefereed preprint. Independent optimization theorists must audit the Lean RAM cost model, formal statement alignment, and constant-factor practicality.

scoreRationale.foundational: Answers one of Steve Smale’s 18 landmark 21st-century mathematical problems open since 1998.
scoreRationale.ripple: Linear programming underpins operations research, economics, control theory, and combinatorial optimization worldwide.
scoreRationale.verification: Includes machine-checked Lean 4 RAM feasibility/optimization proofs, but independent human audit of definitions and paper proof has just begun.
scoreRationale.velocity: Delivered alongside its dual polytope-diameter refutation in a single automated research family.
